div.head: Leis Wl 4
div.ab: Cil ki prendra larrun senz siwte e senz cri, que cil en lest, a ki il avera le damage fait, e il vienge aprés, si est resun, qu’il duinse X sol. de hengwite, e si face la justise a la primere devise.

Cil ki prendra larun sanz suite e sanz cri, que cil en leist, a qui il avrad le damage fait, et vienge pois aprés, si est raisun, que il dunge X solz de hengwite, e [s]i’n face la justice a la primer[ein]e devise.

De latrone capto sine uthes. Si quis latronem siue furem sine clamore et insecutione eius, cui dampnum factum est, ceperit et captum ultra duxerit, dabit X solid. de henwite, et ad primam diuisam faciet de eo iusticiam.
Cil ki prendra larrun senz siwte e senz cri, que cil en lest a ki il avera le damage fait, e il vienge aprés, si est resun qu'il duinse X sol. de hengwite, e si face la justise a la primere devise.

4. Derjenige, welcher einen Dieb festnimmt ohne Folge und ohne Gerüfte, das der, dem jener [Dieb] den Schaden angethan hat, darüber unterlässt: und [dieser Kläg]er kommt (dann I) hernach, so ist Recht, dass dieser 10 Schill. an Strafe für [versäumte] Verhaftung zahle und so das [Straf]gericht (an jenem [Diebe] IL) vollstrecke beim ersten Gerichtstage.

4. He who arrests a thief without pursuit and without hue and cry, which he to whom that [thief] has done the damage omits thereupon: and [this plaint]iff comes (then I) afterwards, then it is right that the latter pay 10 shill. as a penalty for [neglected] arrest and so execute the [penal] judgement (on that [thief] IL) at the first court day.

If a man captures a thief against whom no hue and cry has been raised by the injured man, who afterwards comes forward, then it is right that the latter should pay 10 shillings as a fine for neglecting to arrest the thief, and satisfy the law in this way at the first meeting of the Court.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 254–255 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 496–497, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

L (danach Riley, Schmid, Laughlin) übersieht den Subjektswechsel und missversteht, der Einfänger mache sich strafbar durch längeres Behalten des Gefangenen [sein ultra versteht ‘über die Grenze des Gerichtsbezirks’ Schmid]. Das Nachherkommen des Klägers auch 5, 2. Nicht etwa das ohne Gerüfte durch den Einfänger geschehene Binden wird bestraft, wie Laughlin Essays in Agsax. law 285 meint. Vgl. Gl Strafvollzug 2g

L (followed by Riley, Schmid, Laughlin) overlooks the change of subject and misunderstands the passage to mean that the captor makes himself liable to punishment by keeping the prisoner too long [Schmid takes his ultra to mean ‘beyond the boundary of the court district’]. The plaintiff’s coming afterwards also in 5, 2. It is not, say, the binding done by the captor without hue and cry that is punished, as Laughlin Essays in Agsax. law 285 thinks. Cf. Gl Strafvollzug 2g
Ob zu verbinden mit den 10 Schilling [anderer Währung], die die Anzeige (s. d. Gl 4. 5) belohnen?
Is this to be connected with the 10 shillings [of another currency] that reward information (see that word in Gl 4. 5)?

Vgl. fyrdwite ‘Strafe für versäumtes Heer’; hengwite: Strafe ‘for not keeping a criminal in custody’ Toller; ‘for letting a criminal escape’ Rastal, Spelman, Riley, Sweet; ‘power of imprisonment’ Thorpe Dipl. 657. Antiquare schon 12.—13. Jhs. missverstehen den Terminus ‘Strafe pro latrone sine iudicio suspenso, quite de larun pendu sans serjant le rei, justice faite sanz esward (agard: examinatione); Munim. Gildhal. ed. Riley II 732; Liber rub. Scacc. ed. Hall p. 1036; Stubbs Select char., Gloss. Das Diplom Wilhelms I., das mit hengwite Battle privilegiert, ist bei Davis Reg. Agnorm. n. 22. Strafe für Verbergung des Diebes versteht Stubbs Lect. early Engl. hist. 51

Cf. fyrdwite ‘fine for neglected army service’; hengwite: fine ‘for not keeping a criminal in custody’ Toller; ‘for letting a criminal escape’ Rastal, Spelman, Riley, Sweet; ‘power of imprisonment’ Thorpe Dipl. 657. Antiquaries as early as the 12th–13th cent. misunderstand the term as ‘fine pro latrone sine iudicio suspenso, quite de larun pendu sans serjant le rei, justice faite sanz esward (agard: examinatione); Munim. Gildhal. ed. Riley II 732; Liber rub. Scacc. ed. Hall p. 1036; Stubbs Select char., Gloss. The diploma of William I granting hengwite to Battle as a privilege is in Davis Reg. Agnorm. n. 22. Stubbs Lect. early Engl. hist. 51 takes it as a fine for concealing the thief
